entries.ftd_formula: W₃ := ∫_0^π dx ∫_0^π dy ∫_0^π dz [3 − cos x − cos y − cos z]⁻¹ / π³ = G*²/(2π)

entries.label: t_phys (one tick in seconds)
entries.ftd_formula: t_phys = ℓ_P / (√3 · c) = t_P/√3 (from CFL Courant speed c_lat = 1/√3 + a_phys ≡ ℓ_P + c_phys = 2.998 × 10⁸ m/s: physical c = c_lat·a_phys/t_phys)
entries.calibration_note: Derived (not declared) from a_phys ≡ ℓ_P and the CFL stability constraint c_lat = 1/√3 (which is itself a [THEOREM] from the cubic-lattice wave equation): physical c = c_lat·(a_phys/t_phys) forces t_phys = ℓ_P/(√3·c). Numerically t_phys ≈ 3.11 × 10⁻⁴⁴ s. Corrected 2026-07-08 from √3·ℓ_P/c ≈ 9.34e-44, which placed √3 in the numerator and was inconsistent with c_lat=1/√3 by a factor of 3; see DERIV_DIMENSIONAL_GATE.md.
entries.notes: Once a_phys is fixed, t_phys is fully determined. No additional calibration freedom.

entries.label: m_e (electron mass in MeV/c²) — worked example
entries.ftd_formula: m_e = K_B (lattice value 0.511) × mass-unit (1 MeV/c² per K_B unit) = 0.511 MeV/c²

comparison.method: 0.511 (K_B, 3 sig figs) vs 0.51099895069 (CODATA): bookkeeping match by definition of the anchor. The +2053 ppb gap is purely the precision of K_B as stored in scripts/constants.py — not a physical disagreement.

entries.calibration_note: This is the bridge mechanism: every dimensional FTD prediction reduces to (a) a dimensionless ratio (e.g. m_μ/m_e = 207) times (b) the mass-unit anchor (1 MeV/c² ≡ m_e/K_B). The same pattern applies to lengths (multiply dimensionless ratio by a_phys = ℓ_P) and times (multiply by t_phys = ℓ_P/(√3·c)).
entries.notes: Single worked example. Other dimensional consequences (m_μ in MeV via 207 × m_e, m_p in MeV via m_p/m_e × m_e, etc.) follow the same pattern and are catalogued individually in CATALOG_PARAMETRIC_INSERTIONS.md.
